summary.intent: Refactor a Rust/Tauri desktop application into a Cargo workspace by extracting crypto primitives, domain types, and API client code into separate crates for better modularity and reuse.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 completed successfully (23-01: cipherbox-crypto crate with AES-GCM, AES-CTR, ECIES, Ed25519, HKDF, IPNS primitives). Wave 2 was initiated with two agents spawned in parallel to execute plans 23-02 (cipherbox-core) and 23-03 (cipherbox-api-client).

repo: Project uses a plan-numbered execution system (23-01, 23-02, 23-03) with wave-based parallelism for agent task orchestration.
Codebase has a 'self-check failure marker' concept used to validate agent-executed plan results.
Workspace structure: crates/ directory with subdirectories per crate (crypto/, core/, api-client/).
IPNS name derivation lives in the crypto layer, not the domain/core layer.
The desktop app previously contained inline crypto primitives that needed rewiring to the new workspace crate.
API client code was previously hand-written and contained inline hex constants rather than external test vector files.
workflow: Wave-based execution pattern: complete foundational crates first (Wave 1), then spawn parallel agents for dependent crates (Wave 2).
Spot-checking after each wave includes verifying commits, checking for SUMMARY.md, spot-checking created files, and checking for self-check failure markers.
Agents are spawned in parallel when plans have no inter-dependencies within the same wave.
Cross-language test vectors (Rust/TypeScript parity) are extracted to JSON files rather than kept as inline hex constants.

open_items: Wave 2 agents (23-02, 23-03) were still in-flight at transcript end — outcomes unverified.
Cross-language parity testing between Rust and TypeScript test vectors is being set up but not yet validated.
Any further waves beyond Wave 2 are not yet planned or visible in the transcript.
